name: Anna Petrenko (synthetic)

facts.label: provide professional care in nursing
facts.story: Cares for surgical patients before and after operations: vital signs, pain medication, dressings and watching for complications.

facts.label: deal with emergency care situations
facts.story: Recognised falling blood pressure and confusion in a patient after surgery, called the doctor at once and started fluids per protocol.

facts.label: ensure safety of healthcare users
facts.story: Uses the early warning chart to decide when to call a doctor and writes down times and observations for the team.

facts.label: coordinate care
facts.story: Works with the physiotherapist so that patients move early after surgery.

facts.label: perform venous cannulation
facts.story: Places cannulas and takes blood samples on the surgical ward.

answers.recent_work: I work on a surgical ward at a hospital, as a registered nurse. I take care of patients before and after operations: I check vital signs, manage pain medication, change dressings and watch for complications. I trained and worked ten years in Kyiv in Ukraine, on a city hospital's surgical ward, managing pain medication and changing dressings, and I have worked here for two years after validating my qualification.
answers.example: One night a patient after surgery had low blood pressure and was getting confused. I saw the numbers were changing, called the doctor right away and started fluids, as the protocol says. Bleeding was found and he went back to the operating room. I wrote down the times and what I saw, so the team had the full picture.
answers.tools: We use the hospital patient system for notes and medication, infusion pumps, monitors for blood pressure and oxygen, and wound dressings of different types. I do cannulation and take blood samples. I use the early warning chart to decide when to call a doctor.
answers.people: A ward team of about twenty nurses and assistants, and doctors on rounds. I work closely with the physiotherapist for patients who need to move early after surgery. I also talk with patients' families when they come to visit and explain what is happening, in simple words. My part is the care for my six patients in each shift.
answers.beyond: I also did a course in wound care here in Finland. And in my old hospital I worked one year in emergency, so I stay calm in urgent situations. I have taught new nurses on our ward how to use the infusion pumps.
answers.open_floor: Patients like it when I explain things slowly. I check that they understood by asking them to say it back in their own words.
answers.looking_for: I'd like to stay in surgical or acute care nursing. English is my work language now and I'm learning Finnish, so I can manage simple conversations with patients. Full time, shift work is okay. I can start in two months.

probes: For pain medication I ask the patient to tell me the pain on the ten-point scale every few hours, give the prescribed dose and ask again after forty minutes. If it is still high, I call the doctor, and I write the numbers so the next shift can see how the night went.

For a dressing change I clean my hands, open the dressing, look at the wound edges and drainage, clean with saline, and apply the correct dressing. I note the size and colour in the system, so the next nurse can compare.
